newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end easier on profit-taking after record high.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end easier on profit-taking after record high.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed easier on Monday on profit-taking after hitting a record high of 126.88.

The contract reached the high in mid-afternoon due to continued firmness in cash bonds ahead of Wednesday, the final trading day for cash JGBs for delivery within the current fiscal year ending March 31, traders said. The previous record high was 126.83 hit on January 27.
"Investors refrained from selling ahead of Wednesday," said a senior dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
The June ended at 126.62, down 0.08 from Friday finish.
Turnover was 49,666 contracts. The contract's session low was 126.43.
"Another factor supporting the JGB market was dealers' strong demand for the 190th-193rd 10-year JGBs ahead of Wednesday," the senior dealer said.

Given rate falls in the long-end of the yield curve, the yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB hit a record low for any key JGB of 2.185 percent by midday, traders said. The 182nd JGB was yielding 2.205 percent at 0643 GMT, unchanged from Friday.
The yield of 2.6 percent February 193rd JGB fell to its life low of 2.400 percent on Monday, down from Friday's 2.420.
Scattered cash bond buying from investors was detected this morning, traders said. But a late recovery in Tokyo stocks curbed such buying, and instead triggered light profit-taking.
The key Nikkei stock index finished 129.86 points or 0.72 percent higher at 18,053.50 on Monday, above a psychological support of 18,000.
Traders said some of the long-end JGB buying seen this morning was loss-cut purchases stemming from options trading.
"An unexpectedly sharp rise in cash JGBs since last week has forced some players to buy in order to cut losses on their option trades," said a brokerage house trader.
The yield of the key 182nd JGB has been renewing record lows every day since last Tuesday.
Some traders said they heard a vague, groundless rumour in early afternoon that a senior government official said the period with record low Japanese interest rates was over.
But they said this failed to dampen market sentiment, which remained basically bullish due to a lack of sellers.

"The market ignored the rumour, and this suggested that sentiment was buoyant enough for the key June contract to continue a rally toward another record high," said a senior dealer at another city bank's securities unit.
A dealer at a second-tier securities house said that it is likely that the June contract may challenge 127.00, a psychological resistance point, as early as this week.
